findings.text: The fix matches requirements.md: ChatV2Model.js:40 hands a key that names one of the node's kids to that kid, so `{"p-…":{"t-test-lifecycle":{"complete":{…}}}}` now sets the task's state instead of a stray field on the prompt. It is the smallest change that does it, and I found no simpler route.

ChatV2Model.js:40 only checks `node.kids`, but `children()` (line 89) also counts root-level Tasks/Questions whose `from` is the prompt. A nested write to one of those would still land as a stray field on the prompt. The reported case (task added under the prompt's `tasks`) works, so this is only a gap to watch.

The new test (ChatV2.test.mjs:115-118) starts fixture task t-1761382837000, which the fixture has as `complete`. The only other read of that task is line 35, before the append, so nothing breaks. It does leave the shared fixture task running for any later test.

The readme line (readme.md:23) documents the nested form, and the Chat/v2 module has no doc/ folder or other index that needs updating. Nothing new is unindexed or stale. The task folder (requirements.md, first-review/) is enough for a fresh agent to continue; the "44 passed" and the headless is-complete proof are stated, not saved as files.
